clue.text: Take out a girl

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters of the word before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is told to invite a young woman on a date.
explanation.definitionFit: Kate is a common female forename, so it serves as an example of a girl's name.

clue.text: Overwhelm sweetheart after polite introduction

indicators.note: after places the sweetheart piece behind the introduction piece

parts.note: a bow is a courteous greeting made when introduced
a lover is a sweetheart

explanation.surface: A suitor overwhelms his darling after a courteous first meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: To bowl someone over is an idiom for astonishing or overwhelming them.

clue.text: Die for love without Boatman

indicators.note: without tells us to take the setter's letter out of the word for love

parts.note: passion is intense love
Boatman is the setter, who refers to himself as I

explanation.surface: Someone would perish for love if left without the boatman.
explanation.walkthrough: Boatman is the setter's pseudonym, so 'Boatman' stands for I, as 'this setter' would.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass on is a gentle euphemism for dying.

clue.text: They take arms of trendy lover with taste

parts.note: in means fashionable or trendy
a fan is an enthusiast or lover of something
to try food is to taste it

explanation.surface: Someone with style takes the arms of a fashionable admirer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take arms' looks like romantic arm-in-arm walking; here it means taking up weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: Infantry are foot soldiers, the troops who bear weapons on the ground.

clue.text: Where to relax with (say) cohabitee/husband

indicators.note: say signals that the pieces are spoken and the answer is what they sound like

parts.note: a cohabitee is a live-in partner and a husband is a groom, so together a live-in groom

explanation.surface: A place to unwind with the man one lives with.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken together, LIVE-IN GROOM sounds like the two words of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A living room is the sitting room of a house, where people unwind.

clue.text: See 12
Urn depicting Saint Valentine, the first one taken in by love in Latin verse

indicators.note: taken in by means the following word holds the pieces inside it

parts.note: amor is the Latin word for love, as in the poets

indicators.note: the first picks out the opening letter of the name Valentine

parts.note: a, the indefinite article, means one

explanation.surface: A Valentine's scene in Latin poetry includes an urn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in by' puts V and A inside AMOR, after S.
explanation.definitionFit: A samovar is a Russian metal urn for boiling water for tea.

clue.text: Backing faux naif about marriage vow

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the vow
faux means false, so the letters of naif are put in a false order

parts.note: I do is what is said at a wedding

explanation.surface: A false innocent backs out of a wedding promise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faux' turns NAIF into INAF, and 'about' wraps it around I DO.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in aid of a cause means supporting or backing it.

clue.text: Boy and sweetheart, in love

indicators.note: in places the heart letter inside the word for nothing

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, hence nil
the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter E

explanation.surface: A lad and his darling are in love.
explanation.definitionFit: Neil is a male forename, so it is an example of a boy's name.

clue.text: Mark, notably a single, is desperate

indicators.note: desperate suggests wild disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Mark, a lonely single man, is desperate.
explanation.definitionFit: To signalise something is to make it conspicuous, to mark it out notably.

clue.text: Boatman Rodin sculpted with Lego

indicators.note: sculpted means shaped anew, so the letters are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: A boatman modelled by the sculptor Rodin, built from toy bricks.
explanation.walkthrough: Rodin was a French sculptor, maker of The Kiss; Lego is a toy brick brand.
explanation.definitionFit: A gondolier rows a gondola in Venice, so he is a boatman.

clue.text: Old Labour leader could stay at home and capture lover's heart

indicators.note: capture means the first piece grips another inside it

parts.note: to be in is to stay at home

indicators.note: heart means the middle letter of the word

explanation.surface: A Labour figure might stay home and win his beloved's affection.
explanation.walkthrough: Ernest Bevin was a trade unionist and Labour Foreign Secretary in the 1940s; strictly a leading figure, not party leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernest Bevin was a prominent figure of the British Labour Party in its earlier era.

clue.text: Run away in love, take up and stick to Boatman

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters are read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: lovers who run away together elope
to grab is to take

explanation.surface: Lovers elope, then cling to the boatman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses ELOPE GRAB as a whole to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A bargepole is the long pole used for pushing a barge along.

clue.text: Regret repeat of a loss?

definitions.meaning: the exclamation of dismay when something unwelcome recurs
read as three words, it says something that is no gain

explanation.surface: Lamenting a second defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: The cry is said in dismay at a repeat, and split up it describes a loss.

clue.text: Crazy again — an endearment withheld

indicators.note: withheld means the answer is kept inside the run of words

explanation.surface: Someone silly again keeps back a term of affection.
explanation.definitionFit: Inane means senseless or silly, close to crazy.

clue.text: Lacking warmth? To start, blame old style education

indicators.note: to start picks the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: the three Rs, reading, writing and arithmetic, are traditional basic schooling

explanation.surface: Blame a cold, old-fashioned schooling.
explanation.walkthrough: The three Rs are 'reading, writing and arithmetic', the traditional basics of schooling.
explanation.definitionFit: Brrr is the sound people make when shivering with cold.

clue.text: See 21 down
See 20 Across
Discover endless source of love

indicators.note: endless means the last letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: the heart is traditionally the seat of love

explanation.surface: Find the unending wellspring of love.
explanation.definitionFit: To hear of something is to learn or discover it.

clue.text: Honey, first and dearest, somehow put this behind you and go off safely

definitions.text: put this behind you and go off safely

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the word before it
somehow means the letters are arranged in some other way

explanation.surface: A lover tells the darling to let the past go and leave safely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put this behind you' reads as advice to forget; it is the cushion behind a car seat's occupant.
explanation.definitionFit: A headrest sits behind the occupant's head in a car, protecting them on a journey.

clue.text: Latin trios: trite playing around centre of Alzetto

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters go about the next piece
playing suggests the letters are played about with
centre of picks the middle three letters of the name

explanation.surface: Italian trio pieces played tritely around a musician named Alzetto.
explanation.walkthrough: Terzetti is really Italian, not Latin; 'Latin' here is loose for a Romance language.
explanation.definitionFit: Terzetti is the plural of terzetto, an Italian word for a vocal trio.

clue.text: What's the pinnacle of eathtern thought?

parts.note: Zen is a school of Eastern Buddhist thought, the clue's lisp spelling eastern
the clue lisps throughout, so the 's (is) of this phrase comes out lisped too

explanation.surface: A lisping question about the height of Eastern philosophy.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue lisps ('eathtern'), so 'Zen is' becomes ZEN ITH.
explanation.definitionFit: The zenith is the highest point, a synonym of peak or pinnacle.

clue.text: Modern British setting for Rodin's lovers in gentle symbol of love

indicators.note: in means the gallery is placed inside the other piece

parts.note: a soft heart is a tender emblem of affection
Rodin's sculpture The Kiss is displayed at Tate Britain, a London gallery

explanation.surface: A gallery is home to Rodin's embracing lovers among symbols of affection.
explanation.walkthrough: Tate Britain is a London art gallery, where a version of The Kiss is housed.
explanation.definitionFit: State of the art describes the most modern, up-to-date technology.

clue.text: Instructed to attack in tennis game

indicators.note: game, as in a game leg, suggests something lame or askew, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A player told to go on the attack during a tennis match.
explanation.definitionFit: Troops sent in are ordered to go into an attack.

clue.text: Old Jewish court and shrine rebuilt

indicators.note: rebuilt means the letters are put together again in a new form

explanation.surface: A historic court and a shrine are reconstructed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sanhedrin was the supreme council and court of ancient Jerusalem.

clue.text: Interest in obscene and difficult work about Latin writer (last in trilogy)

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes around the writer

parts.note: a slog is hard, tiring work
Cato was a Roman author

indicators.note: last in picks the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A trilogy's final book about a Roman author is filthy and heavy going.
explanation.definitionFit: Scatology is a preoccupation with excrement and obscene matters.

clue.text: See 5
Sound of animal from an empty pen?

parts.note: an empty thing holds nothing, shown as the round zero O
to pen a letter is to ink it

explanation.surface: A noise from a vacant pigsty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pen' suggests a sty for livestock; here it is a writing verb.
explanation.definitionFit: An oink is the grunt a pig makes.

clue.text: Change of heart for rotter, untouched by love

indicators.note: the central letters swap places, a change at the heart of the word

parts.note: a rat is a contemptible person, a rotter
pure means untouched or unsullied

explanation.surface: A scoundrel has a change of heart, never touched by romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change of heart' moves the T of RATPURE past the central P.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapture is ecstatic joy, the delight of being in love.

clue.text: A thousand singles make mouth music, like Rodin's lovers

parts.note: K stands for a thousand
singles are ones, written as Roman I's
to sing is to make music with the mouth

explanation.surface: Lots of unattached people make music with their lips, as Rodin's couple do.
explanation.walkthrough: Rodin's famous sculpture of two lovers is called The Kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: Rodin's lovers are shown in an embrace with lips meeting, as in kissing.
